title: Motherson plans a Rs 3,491 crore car parts plant in Yamuna City near Jewar airport
subtitle: YEIDA gave the car parts maker a letter of intent for 150 acres on 23 October. Here is what that letter means and who Motherson really is.
content_html:
Picture a huge, empty stretch of land, 150 acres big, a short drive from India's newest big airport. Soon, it could be full of machines making the wires, mirrors and lights that go inside your family car. On Friday, 23 October 2026, the company behind that plan, Samvardhana Motherson International, got a letter of intent for 150 acres in Yamuna City from the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority, or YEIDA.

The plan is worth Rs 3,491 crore. That is more money than most people can imagine, so here is the simple version: who Motherson is, what this letter means, and why so many companies now want land near Jewar.

What exactly happened on Friday?

YEIDA is the government body that plans and hands out land for factories and homes along the Yamuna Expressway. A YEIDA official said the company will be given 150 acres in Sectors 6 and 7 of Yamuna City, and that the letter was issued on Friday.

The new unit will make car parts. The list includes wiring harnesses, PVC-covered wires, rear-view mirrors, car lighting, precision metal parts, exhaust systems and even parts for aircraft. It will also have space for injection moulding, tool making, assembly and testing, Navbharat Times reported.

What is a letter of intent?

Think of a busy restaurant. You call ahead, and the manager puts a "reserved" card on a table for you. You have not eaten yet and the bill is not paid, but everyone knows that table is yours. A letter of intent works a bit like that card. It tells the company that the land is set aside for its project. The full handover and the paperwork come after.

So this is an early but real step. It is not a finished factory. Urban Acres pointed out that no construction start date, opening date or finish deadline has been shared yet.

Who is Motherson, and why have you never heard of it?

You may never have seen the name Motherson on a car. That is because it is a supplier. It makes parts that go into cars sold by many different brands. Think of a tailor who stitches shirts for ten different clothes shops. Each shop puts its own label on the shirt, but the same tailor made all of them.

The name has a sweet story behind it. In 1975, a 19-year-old named Vivek Chaand Sehgal started a business with his mother, Swaran Lata Sehgal. They called it Motherson, meaning mother and son, according to the Financial Express. It began as a small silver trading business. By 1977 it had a cable factory in Noida.

The big break came in 1983. India was getting the Maruti 800, its first affordable locally assembled car. Motherson made the car's wiring harness, and later teamed up with Japan's Sumitomo, the Financial Express story says.

What is a wiring harness? Think of it as the nerves of a car. It is a big bundle of wires that carries power and signals from the battery to the lights, the horn, the music system and the dashboard. Without it, a car is just a metal box that cannot even blink an indicator.

Today Motherson's registered office is in Mumbai and its corporate office is in Noida, Navbharat Times noted. So this new plant is close to home.

Where will the Rs 3,491 crore go?

The money is split into four parts, Federal Bharat reported, citing the company's plan:

  • Plant and machinery: Rs 1,928 crore. This is the biggest piece, for the machines that cut, mould and assemble parts.
  • Buildings: Rs 997 crore, for the factory buildings.
  • Utilities: Rs 383 crore. Utilities are the basic services every building needs, like power lines, water and drainage.
  • Land: Rs 183 crore.

Add them up: 1,928 plus 997 plus 383 plus 183 makes exactly 3,491. More than half the money goes to machines. That tells you machines are the heart of this plan.

Where does the money come from? The company plans to fund it from internal accruals, the same Federal Bharat report said. That is a fancy way of saying it will use money it has already earned and saved. Imagine buying a new cycle with your own saved pocket money instead of borrowing from a friend.

This is also a greenfield project. That means building a brand new plant on empty land, from scratch. It is like setting up a new shop on an empty plot instead of renting an old one and repainting it.

How many people could find work there?

The company's plan expects the project to create work for 15,000 to 20,000 people over the next five years. Keep in mind that this is an estimate, not a promise. It is spread over five years, and it does not say how many people will work inside the plant itself and how many in related work like transport and packing.

Why does everyone want land near Jewar?

One big reason is the new Noida International Airport at Jewar. Its first phase was inaugurated on 28 March 2026, and it is meant to work alongside Delhi's main airport.

Navbharat Times wrote that since the airport came up, the YEIDA area has become more important for industry and trade, with better roads and growing facilities pulling companies in. In simple words, good roads and a big airport nearby make a place more attractive for factories.

Think of it like opening a samosa stall right outside a busy railway station. More people, more movement, more chances to sell.

What happens next?

The letter is the first confirmed milestone. What comes next depends on Motherson actually building the plant, and no timetable has been shared yet. If the plan goes as written, a quiet piece of land near Jewar could one day be sending wires, mirrors and lights to car factories across the country.
